name: rdkit
why: Chemoinformatics toolkit for molecules is real science you can run at home, but it is a large, widely known library.

brief.what_it_is: RDKit is an open-source cheminformatics and machine-learning library, written mainly in C++ with Python bindings. It works on molecules: 2D and 3D molecular operations, substructure and similarity searching, and generation of descriptors and fingerprints for machine learning. It can also run as a PostgreSQL molecular database cartridge, and it ships wrappers for Java, C#, and JavaScript. Input is molecules and molecular data; output is computed properties, fingerprints, search results, and molecule objects.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes it simply as a collection of cheminformatics and machine-learning software. The homepage calls it an open-source cheminformatics library and links to a yearly user group meeting where people present their work with it.
brief.how_it_works: The core data structures and algorithms are in C++. Python 3 bindings are generated with Boost.Python, Java and C# wrappers with SWIG, and JavaScript and CFFI wrappers with emscripten and CFFI respectively. The README does not describe the internals of molecule representation beyond that.

commands_seen.context: The README's recommended install path for Python users who use conda. Shown as the first step before the Getting Started in Python guide.

brief.install_notes: The README recommends conda: conda install -c conda-forge rdkit. A more detailed guide is in Docs/Book/Install.md in the repository. The Homebrew formula is contributed by Eddie Cao, as listed on the homepage. The Homebrew caveat says you may need to set RDBASE, for example export RDBASE=$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/rdkit/share/RDKit. That line comes from the Homebrew metadata, not from the README I read. Homebrew metadata lists no executables, so this is a library to import, not a command-line tool.
brief.standout: It is a library rather than an app, so the interesting part is what you can do from Python: fingerprints, substructure search, and a PostgreSQL cartridge that brings chemical search into a database. The BSD license is business-friendly, and the project has a long run of annual user meetings with the materials published online.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as I can tell. The GitHub README shows an active Azure build badge and a Zenodo DOI badge, and it lists UGMs through 2024. I did not see a last-release or last-commit date on the pages I read, so I cannot confirm the date of the latest release.
brief.caveats: The homepage is mostly a list of links and gives little description. Installing from source is not covered in the README itself; it points to Docs/Book/Install.md. The Homebrew path needs the RDBASE setting. The scout note calls RDKit large and widely known; I did not verify that beyond the README. The homepage links to a commercial support provider, T5 Informatics GmbH.
quotes: The RDKit is a collection of cheminformatics and machine-learning software written in C++ and Python.
